did.unittitle: Collection of material about the Peace and Freedom Party
did.abstract: Collection consists of ephemeral materials, internal papers, and campaign literature relating to the Peace and Freedom Party.

accessrestrict.head: Conditions Governing Access
accessrestrict.p: Portions of collection unprocessed. Please see LSC's Access to Unprocessed Collections Policy for more information about levels of discovery and access of special collections materials and to register interest in unprocessed collections.

processinfo.head: Processing Information
processinfo.p: Collections are processed to a variety of levels depending on the work necessary to make them usable, their perceived user interest and research value, availability of staff and resources, and competing priorities. Library Special Collections provides a standard level of preservation and access for all collections and, when time and resources permit, conducts more intensive processing. These materials have been arranged and described according to national and local standards and best practices.

We are committed to providing ethical, inclusive, and anti-racist description of the materials we steward, and to remediating existing description of our materials that contains language that may be offensive or cause harm. We invite you to submit feedback about how our collections are described, and how they could be described more accurately, by filling out the form located on our website: Report Problematic Content and Description in UCLA's Library Collections and Archives.

bioghist.head: Biographical / Historical
bioghist.p: The Peace and Freedom Party in California was officially founded at a convention in Sacramento, California, in 1968. It successfully initiated a statewide campaign to participate in the 1968 election as a recognized third party. Local clubs and chapters were subsequently established throughout the state. The objective of the Party was to promote revolutionary change in the country; it represented an effort to build a durable, grass-roots, radical political party in the United States. Elements of the Peace and Freedom platform during this time include opposition to the Vietnam War and the draft, dissatisfaction with the Lyndon Johnson administration, lack of faith in the two-party system, and the desire to end racism in the United States. Peace and Freedom members allied themselves with other radical movements of the 1960s, including those for anti-war, civil liberties, civil rights, free speech, women's rights and student protest activities.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: The order of the material as originally donated has been maintained. Many folders contain several different types of material from both series. Material in boxes 1 and 3-10 donated by Len Evans; material in boxes 12-14 donated by Lewis McCammon; boxes 2 and 11 contain oversize material from both donors.
